newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai B share index hits record low.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai B share index hits record low.

text.p: Shanghai's B share index lost 0.406 points or 0.86 percent in early afternoon on Wednesday to hit a record low of 46.729 points, its second record low in a week.
The low beat the previous record of 46.731 points set on Thursday last week.
Brokers said overseas liquidation continued today, with the market in deep depression and seeing no sign of short-term recovery due to a lack of government support and poor company results.
Beijing has repeatedly re-affirmed a ban on domestic trading in B shares, weakening market sentiment, they said.
"With most domestic investors having withdrawn from the market, thin liquidation by overseas investors has continuously depressed the index in the past few weeks," said one broker.
Many key Shanghai B share companies have reported sharp falls in profits in the past two years, disheartening foreign investors, brokers said.
"Most foreigners have stopped trading on the market, with those still there looking for opportunities to pull out," said a second broker.
